policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads simply 'And he spake a parable unto them', with no 'also'. The added kai of r01 is adverbial ('spake also a parable'), and ASV does render that kai as 'also' where it stands at 18:9 ('And he spake also this parable'). Its absence here distinguishes the shorter base reading.
ASV renders the indirect object 'unto them', unitalicized, answering autous; r01 omits the pronoun.

Imperfect ethelen against aorist ethelesen. ASV 'And he would not for a while' expresses the durative sense through the adverbial 'for a while' (epi chronon), which stands in both readings; English 'would not' fits either aspect and no note is mapped here.
Pure word order of tauta and de, both post-positive and untranslated as a sequence; ASV 'but afterward he said within himself' cannot show the Greek order.

ASV 'nor regard man' coordinates a negated clause, which both readings do: oude directly, and kai ... ouk of r01 idiomatically (KJV renders that same Byzantine text 'nor regard man'). The English negative conjunction does not separate them.
Dative auto against pros auton, both simply 'to him' in ASV 'that cry to him day and night'; the mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns the following clause's English wording only.

ASV renders a finite verb in an independent clause coordinated with the question: 'and yet he is longsuffering over them?' That answers indicative makrothumei; the participle makrothumon of r01 yields a subordinate clause ('though he bear long with them', KJV). The alternative_rendering note likewise offers a finite clause, 'and is he slow to punish on their behalf?'
ASV 'And he spake also this parable' renders the adverbial kai as 'also'; r01 omits it.

Article on heis. ASV 'the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican' is the fixed English correlative for heis ... ho heteros and would be written the same with or without the article; the mapped note is a cross-reference about 'publican', not this variant.
Word order of pros heauton and tauta only; ASV 'prayed thus with himself' contains both elements and cannot show their Greek sequence.
hosper against hos, both rendered by the same comparative 'as' in 'that I am not as the rest of men'.
Orthographic and conjugational variation of the same verb (apodekato / apodekateuo), identical in sense; ASV 'I give tithes of all that I get' cannot distinguish them.
ASV opens the verse 'But the publican', an adversative rendering de; r01 substitutes kai, which ASV would render 'And' (so KJV, 'And the publican'). The conjunction is visible in the English.
Word order of eparai relative to eis ton ouranon; English 'lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven' fixes its own order and cannot report the Greek one.
ASV 'but smote his breast' takes the breast as a bare direct object. r01's added eis gives a prepositional phrase, rendered 'smote upon his breast' (so KJV); ASV has no 'upon'.
autou against reflexive heautou, both rendered 'his' in 'his breast'; ASV does not mark the reflexive here.

par' ekeinon against e gar ekeinos. Both yield ASV's 'justified rather than the other: for every one...' - the comparison plus a causal connective before pas - so the English does not separate the constructions.
Imperfect epetimon against aorist epetimesan; ASV 'they rebuked them' is a simple past that serves either aspect.

ASV 'But Jesus called them unto him, saying' has a finite main verb followed by a participle, matching prosekalesato ... legon. r01's aorist participle plus finite eipen gives 'having called them ... said' (KJV 'called them unto him, and said').
an against ean in the indefinite relative clause; both are 'whosoever shall not receive' in English.

ASV 'Honor thy father and mother' carries a single unitalicized possessive, answering ton patera sou kai ten metera. r01's added sou after metera gives a second possessive, 'thy father and thy mother' (so KJV here).
Active ephulaxa against middle ephulaxamen of the same verb; ASV 'have I observed' renders either without distinction.
ASV 'from my youth up' has an unitalicized possessive answering mou; r01 omits the pronoun.

ASV 'And when Jesus heard it' supplies a bare 'it' for the absolute participle. Where tauta is in the text ASV renders it 'these things' (so the next verse, 18:23, 'But when he heard these things'), and KJV, following the longer text here, likewise reads 'heard these things'. The shorter base reading is what ASV's 'it' reflects.
Anarthrous plural, articular plural, and singular ouranoi all appear in English as 'treasure in heaven'; ASV neither pluralizes nor articulates heaven, so none of the three is excluded.
egenethe against egeneto, alternative aorists of ginomai with the same sense; ASV 'he became exceeding sorrowful' does not distinguish them.
ASV reads only 'And Jesus seeing him said'. r01's added perilupon genomenon supplies the object clause rendered 'that he was very sorrowful' (so KJV); ASV has nothing answering it.

The readings differ in the verb (eisporeuontai / eiseleusontai) and its position relative to the prepositional phrase. ASV 'How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!' uses one English verb 'enter' for either Greek verb and fixes English order; nothing here selects.
trematos belones against trumalias raphidos, two idioms for the same object; ASV renders both as 'a needle's eye'.
Word order of estin and para to theo only; ASV 'are possible with God' cannot report the Greek sequence.
Article with the proper name Petros, which English does not represent: 'And Peter said' either way. The mapped note is an alternative_rendering about ta idia, not this unit.
ASV 'we have left our own' with the note 'Or, our own homes' renders ta idia; r01 reads aphekamen panta, 'we have left all' (so KJV). The ASV wording and its mapped note both answer the base reading.
ASV lists 'house, or wife, or brethren, or parents, or children' - wife, brethren, parents in that sequence, the base order. r01 inverts it to parents, brethren, wife.
ouchi against ou, emphatic and plain forms of the same negative; ASV 'who shall not receive' renders either.
apolabe against labe; ASV 'receive' serves the simple and compound verb alike and marks no intensive force.
The two Greek forms of the city's name are both 'Jerusalem' in ASV.
epaiton against prosaiton, synonymous participles both rendered 'begging'.
The added an makes the clause a potential optative; ASV's indirect question 'he inquired what this meant' reads the same with or without it.
sigese against siopese, synonyms both rendered by ASV's 'that he should hold his peace'.
Article with Iesous, which English does not represent: 'And Jesus stood' either way.

ASV moves straight from 'he asked him,' at the end of 18:40 into the direct question, with no participle of speaking. r01's legon is rendered 'saying' (KJV 'he asked him, Saying, What wilt thou'), and ASV has none.
